security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by documentation, detection rules, and secure examples. The ping example permits argument injection, while semantic review found unsafe path containment, suppressed CI failures, swallowed scanner errors, and unpinned tooling.

remediation.issue: User input can inject ping options.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the value as an IP address or hostname, reject leading dashes, and place -- before the destination where supported.

remediation.issue: The path containment example uses a string prefix check.
remediation.suggestion: Use pathlib.Path.resolve with is_relative_to, or os.path.commonpath, and reject paths outside the resolved allowed directory.

remediation.issue: CI scanner commands ignore every nonzero exit status.
remediation.suggestion: Remove || true and define explicit policies for findings, tool errors, and report upload behavior.

remediation.issue: Semgrep exceptions are swallowed without scan status.
remediation.suggestion: Record ruleset failures and return a failed or partial status. Fail closed when required scans cannot complete.

remediation.issue: Security tools and CI actions are not immutably pinned.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions and action commit hashes, then update them through a reviewed dependency process.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Path Containment Check
semantic_findings.description: The secure path example uses string startswith for containment. A sibling path sharing the allowed prefix can pass this check and permit unintended file access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly compares canonical path strings by prefix, a known boundary error when paths such as uploads-other share the allowed prefix.

semantic_findings.title: SAST CI Failures Are Suppressed
semantic_findings.description: The CI examples append || true to scanner commands. Findings, crashes, or configuration errors therefore cannot fail the security job.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both CI examples explicitly convert every nonzero scanner exit into success, defeating enforcement and masking operational failures.

semantic_findings.title: Scanner Errors Produce Incomplete Results
semantic_findings.description: The scanner catches every Semgrep exception, prints it, and continues. Callers can receive a normal summary without knowing that one or more rulesets failed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The broad exception handler records no failure state and does not rethrow, while the outer workflow always generates a summary.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Security Tool Installation
semantic_findings.description: Installation examples fetch current package and action versions without immutable pins. A compromised or incompatible release could affect CI execution and scan integrity.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples install Bandit, Semgrep, and ESLint without versions and reference GitHub Actions by mutable major tags rather than commit hashes.

content.user_title: Scan Source Code for Security Vulnerabilities
content.value_statement: Manual security review can miss recurring vulnerabilities across large, mixed-language repositories. This skill configures SAST tools, triages findings, and suggests focused remediations.
actual_capabilities: Selects SAST tools for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Ruby, Go, and Rust.
Provides Bandit, Semgrep, ESLint Security, and framework configuration examples.
Reviews SQL injection, XSS, secrets, path traversal, deserialization, and command injection patterns.
Drafts custom Semgrep rules for organization-specific security policies.
Summarizes findings by severity and proposes secure coding changes.
Provides GitHub Actions and GitLab CI integration examples.
limitations: It does not perform runtime penetration testing or dynamic application security testing.
Scanner quality depends on installed tools, selected rulesets, and repository access.
Generated findings require human validation for exploitability and business impact.
Example configurations need adaptation before use in production pipelines.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Identify security-sensitive changes, run relevant SAST checks, and prioritize actionable findings before merge.

use_cases.title: Build a Security Pipeline
use_cases.description: Choose scanners, configure CI jobs, preserve reports, and define clear failure policies.

use_cases.title: Create Custom Detection Rules
use_cases.description: Translate internal secure coding requirements into focused Semgrep rules with testable examples.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Repository Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify this repository's languages and frameworks. Recommend suitable SAST tools and list the commands needed for an initial scan.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Scanner Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these SAST findings. Remove clear false positives, rank exploitable issues by severity, and explain each recommended fix.

prompt_templates.title: Secure a Framework
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this Django, Flask, or Express configuration for common security weaknesses. Provide framework-specific fixes and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a SAST Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-language SAST pipeline for this repository. Include tool selection, pinned dependencies, custom rules, baselines, failure policies, and report retention.

output_examples.input: Review a Python API for SQL injection and command injection.
output: High: User input reaches a shell command without strict argument validation.
High: A query uses string formatting instead of parameters.
Recommendation: Use argument arrays, input allowlists, and parameterized queries.

output_examples.input: Choose SAST tools for a TypeScript and Python repository.
output_examples.output: Use Semgrep across both languages, Bandit for Python, and ESLint Security for TypeScript. Run each tool in CI with pinned versions.

output_examples.input: Summarize a scan containing repeated findings.
output_examples.output: Group duplicates by root cause, preserve affected locations, prioritize reachable high-impact issues, and mark uncertain results for manual review.

best_practices: Run scanners with pinned versions and reviewed rulesets in isolated CI environments.
Validate findings against data flow, reachability, and application context before changing production code.
Fail closed on scanner errors while separating tool failures from confirmed vulnerability policy violations.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every scanner match as an exploitable vulnerability.
Do not suppress scanner exit codes without recording and evaluating the failure.
Do not upload proprietary source code to external scanning services without approval.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Ruby, PHP, Go, and Rust, depending on available scanners.

faq.question: Does this replace penetration testing?
faq.answer: No. SAST examines source code and should complement runtime testing, threat modeling, and expert review.

faq.question: Can it run in CI?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes GitHub Actions and GitLab CI patterns that should be hardened before production use.

faq.question: How should false positives be handled?
faq.answer: Validate reachability and context, document accepted risk, and tune rules narrowly without hiding unrelated findings.

faq.question: Can it create custom rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides Semgrep rule patterns that can be adapted to internal policies and tested against representative code.

faq.question: Does it handle secrets scanning?
faq.answer: It covers basic hardcoded secret patterns. Dedicated secret scanners remain necessary for deeper history and credential analysis.
